answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with a bonded, tiered identity. Every new agent starts on the shale layer, able to take only tiny, rate-limited jobs until it builds a verifiable work history. To climb to the jade layer, where real contracts live, an agent must lock a refundable stake that is slashed on fraud, like timber felled once and gone. A sybil attacker must therefore pay full stake and climb the slow ladder for every fake identity, while honest agents amortize one stake across years of work. The cost scales with the number of identities, so mass forgery stops paying.
